summary: Reader-facing ordered irrigation lifecycle, per-event units, contextual source evidence and Mediterranean/Almería carob communities.

topics.label: Nursery watering
topics.description: Before field planting, maintain suitable substrate moisture and adapt irrigation to the growing stage, stock, climate and hardening programme. LIFE NIEBLAS documents a project nursery regime; the carob handbook does not prescribe a universal numerical nursery dose.

aspects.Amount: LIFE NIEBLAS: approximately 0.3 L/plant/event as an average calculated from 30 L for 100 plants. Carob handbook: Not specified in this source.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: LIFE: twice weekly. Carob: frequent irrigation during growth; more intense, spaced applications during hardening, adapted to weather.
aspects.Applicable period: Nursery growth and preconditioning before planting; no universal calendar.
aspects.Age and stock: Nursery one-season stock (1+0) and two-season grafted stock (1+1) have different programmes. These ages are not years since field planting.
aspects.Limitations: A 1 L or 3 L pot is container capacity, not water dose. Up to 10% leaching describes drainage, not litres per plant. A batch average is not a measured individual dose.

topics.label: Settlement watering
topics.description: The first water supplied immediately after field planting helps settle the planted root zone. Keep this single purpose separate from maintenance and support throughout the following establishment years.

aspects.Purpose: First watering immediately after field planting.
aspects.Amount: LIFE: 10–15 L/plant/event; Cocoon also receives a separate 20 L reservoir fill.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: At planting. Subsequent watering is classified by its purpose.
aspects.Applicable period: The planting date; a universal month is Not specified in this source.
aspects.Age and stock: Newly field-planted seedlings, which may already have spent one or more seasons in a nursery.
aspects.Limitations: LIFE project choices across methods, not a universal carob dose. Tank filling is a separate quantity. “Establishment watering” may span several years and is broader than settlement.

topics.label: Summer maintenance watering
topics.description: Recurring watering during summer or another difficult period follows a documented interval or trigger. Read the method, site, season and establishment period together rather than selecting a dose on its own.

aspects.Purpose: Recurring water during difficult seasonal conditions.
aspects.Amount: LIFE traditional/Cocoon: 15 L/plant/event; IND: 10 L/plant/event. “SAD”: approximately 15 L/plant/event. Carob examples have their own doses.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: Traditional/Cocoon/IND: monthly. “SAD”: tank filling triggers discharge; the project describes about every three weeks, not a guaranteed interval.
aspects.Applicable period: LIFE traditional/Cocoon/IND: July–September inclusive. SAD calendar season: Not specified in this source.
aspects.Age and stock: LIFE method passages discuss the first field year. Carob examples include the first two summers; this does not establish a universal stopping age.
aspects.Limitations: The first-year water-network estimate (about 40 L/plant, around 12.5 L/event) is a storage-planning estimate, separate from method-specific schedules. Seasonal totals cannot supply a dose by themselves.

topics.label: Support watering during stress
topics.description: Additional water may be considered when weather, soil moisture or plant condition indicates stress. It can overlap the establishment and maintenance periods; being listed last does not make it a final lifecycle stage.

aspects.Purpose: Respond to unusually dry weather, heat or plant stress.
aspects.Amount: LIFE: Not specified in this source. MR2: Not specified in this source. El Triguero reports 50 L/plant/event as a site-specific emergency practice.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: LIFE: monitor forecasts and plant condition; prolonged lack of rain or widespread yellow/dry symptoms can prompt watering. El Triguero reports monthly emergency watering.
aspects.Applicable period: When the stated conditions occur; no universal seasonal calendar.
aspects.Age and stock: May overlap the field establishment years and maintenance. No general dose by plant age or automatic stopping age is supplied.
aspects.Limitations: Unknown amount is not zero. An observed emergency regime at one finca is not a general prescription for all carob or Almería sites.

topics.label: SAD (LIFE maintenance wording)
topics.description: The maintenance passage uses SAD for a fog-water tank system that releases about 15 L/plant/event when full, at a reported interval of about three weeks. The acronym is not expanded there. A correspondence with the AFDS mechanism is curated, not a verified expansion.

topics.label: Autonomous Fluid Discharge System (AFDS)
topics.description: A tank-level-triggered device discharges collected water through an irrigation network without electrical energy. Intervals depend on fog-water supply, tank settings and the network. The source maintenance label SAD is linked by an explicitly curated correspondence.

topics.label: Mediterranean carob associations
topics.description: General overview of Mediterranean vegetation associated with carob in section 1.2, page 18. The named companions are not one formal botanical association, a worldwide recipe or proof that every species occurs together. Read the Almería examples for local observations.

topics.label: Carob communities in Almería
topics.description: Regional examples of carob-associated vegetation in arid and semiarid Almería. Mastic and wild olive are observed at La Alcantarilla and La Tórtola; wider MR2 companions and potential habitats have different evidence. Las Labores is a managed restoration planting replacing almond and olive. These are explanatory regional groupings, not a single formal association.

topics.label: Cornical scrub
topics.description: Cornicales are named among the arid settings in the MR2 discussion. This habitat label alone does not establish a particular species identification or its occurrence at a finca.

topics.label: Carob restoration of degraded areas (MR1)
topics.description: MR1 uses carob with other forest species for soil protection and restoration of degraded Mediterranean areas. Restoration layouts, genetic diversity and microsite selection differ from production-oriented plantings.

topics.label: Carob landscape diversification (MR3)
topics.description: The introductory passage describes diversification of low-productivity agricultural landscapes, particularly olive and almond areas, where carob can occur with other forest species and xerophytic shrubs. Only the opening on page 137 is covered here.

findings.label: Nursery batch quantity and its calculated average
findings.text: LIFE NIEBLAS describes watering the nursery twice a week with around 30 L for 100 plants. Dividing the documented batch quantity by its plant count gives an average 0.3 L/plant/event; the source does not report individually metered doses or identify this as a carob-specific requirement.

findings.label: LIFE summer schedules retain method and season
findings.text: The project choices are 15 L/plant/event monthly July–September for traditional planting and Cocoon, and 10 L/plant/event on that schedule for IND. The passage labelled SAD describes about 15 L/plant/event every three weeks when the fog-water tank fills. Its timing depends on collection, and the passage does not specify its calendar season.

findings.label: First field year differs from nursery age
findings.text: Traditional, Cocoon and individual fog collector method descriptions discuss irrigation in the first year after field planting, with amounts adapted to site, species and soil moisture. Nursery age or stock format is a different measure. No universal age for stopping irrigation is given.

findings.label: A first-year storage estimate is not a method dose
findings.text: The water-network section estimates about 40 L/plant for first-year summer provision, around 12.5 L per irrigation across three important irrigations, and illustrates 120,000 L storage for 3,000 plants. These are approximate storage-planning figures; preserve them separately from the 15/10 L project maintenance regimes and do not force the rounded figures into exact agreement.

findings.label: Carob nursery irrigation changes with development
findings.text: Tables 4.4–4.5b describe humid germination, frequent early watering without leaching, active growth watering with up to 10% leaching, and spaced intense irrigation during preconditioning to moderate water stress. Page 79 says nursery-specific schedules prevent specific general recommendations. No litres-per-plant dose is supplied.

findings.label: Carob establishment spans years, not a single settlement event
findings.text: The general planting recommendations describe 3–5 years of establishment and advise 1–5 summer waterings during the first five years, without litres per event or an explicit annual allocation. Preserve that wording without inventing a per-year frequency or a universal dose.

findings.label: AFDS uses a tank level, not a guaranteed calendar
findings.text: AFDS discharges automatically once the tank reaches a level and resets after emptying. Cycle time depends on collection, tank settings and network characteristics. Internal installation is compact but less accessible; external installation permits level adjustment and easier maintenance, with more exposure and blockage risk.

findings.label: Measure water and plant counts by purpose
findings.text: The manual separates nursery, settlement, maintenance, support, waste and other water. Hose watering can be measured from before/after quantities and plant counts; AFDS monitoring records discharge count, frequency and volume. Total water use and water per surviving tree are different metrics from an event dose.

findings.label: Las Labores: dryland crops and a restoration transition
findings.text: Las Labores (Albox) has 200–400 mm annual rainfall, Mediterranean IV1 climate, coldest-month minimum 2–4°C, warmest-month maximum 32–36°C, annual mean 17–19°C, evapotranspiration 900–1000 mm/year, shallow calcareous soils and rocky outcrops. The landscape is dominated by dryland woody crops. Carob was planted in 2010 at 6 × 6 m in areas of dead almond trees, as almond and olive productivity declined.

findings.label: Las Labores: planting, protection and grafting
findings.text: The case uses nursery plants about 1 m high, manual 40 × 40 × 40 cm holes, perforated 60 cm shelters, tutors, formative pruning and tractor cultivation every three years. It reports grafting local hermaphrodite cultivars in autumn 2024. These are case practices, distinct from the MR1 summary table.

findings.label: Las Labores: 400 litres is a seasonal total
findings.text: Deficit drip irrigation is reported from May to September, with a total of 400 L/plant over that period. The number of events and dose per event are not specified. The seasonal total must not be imported as 400 L/plant/event.

findings.label: Las Labores: reported establishment and fruit observations
findings.text: The manual reports low losses, good condition, heights 3–5 m and normal diameters 10–25 cm, with alternate bearing. Table 5.16 (summer 2023) gives pod length 12.40 cm, pod weight 13.56 g, seed yield 16.39% and 100-seed weight 17.73 g. Its claim about production four years after grafting conflicts with the reported autumn-2024 grafting and harvest chronology; retain that unresolved.

findings.label: La Alcantarilla: carob facilitates observed shrub establishment
findings.text: A seminatural carob population around houses and a stream has expanded irregularly along paths, irrigation channels and streams. Lentisco and acebuche have established under carob protection. Care is limited mainly to fruit collection. Alternate bearing is moderate, but crops are small or absent in most years. This is not a quantified planting trial.

findings.label: La Alcantarilla: fruit table and climatic context
findings.text: Table 5.20 gives rainfall 200–300 mm/year, minimum temperature of the coldest month >6°C, maximum of warmest month 28–32°C, mean annual temperature 17–19°C and evapotranspiration 900–1000 mm/year. Table 5.21 (summers 2022/2023) gives pod length 14.2 cm, pod weight 8.66 g, seed yield 16.39% and 100-seed weight 13.90 g; sample size is not supplied.

findings.label: La Tórtola: potential scrub differs from the present landscape
findings.text: La Tórtola (Níjar) has Mediterranean IV3 climate, rainfall 200–300 mm/year and potential lentiscares/jujube thorn scrub, while espartales dominate the current surrounding landscape. Table 5.22 gives coldest-month minimum >6°C, warmest-month maximum 28–32°C, annual mean 17–19°C and evapotranspiration 900–1000 mm/year.

findings.label: La Tórtola: naturalized vegetation and very low production
findings.text: Abandonment of earlier agricultural and livestock activity allowed lentisco and acebuche to establish with carob, creating more luxuriant vegetation than surrounding areas. The population is described as fully naturalized without cultural treatments. Trees range from about 1 to 10 m, with variable diameters, very high alternate bearing and practically no production. Irrigation quantity/frequency is not specified; do not turn absence of a stated regime into zero.

findings.label: MR1 restoration guidance retains its own assumptions
findings.text: MR1 recommends diverse, appropriate-provenance forest material, favourable deeper/moister microsites, autumn planting and low-density restoration layouts. Page 123 describes <350 trees/ha, page 124 gives <100 in generic protective restoration, and Table 5.14 describes enrichment <200. The table says no irrigation; this summary does not negate watering documented at Las Labores.

findings.label: MR1 reports variable survival in earlier restoration
findings.text: The narrative reports survival ranges of 18–30% at Guadiamar, 0–65% in Córdoba and 40–60% in Almería, citing earlier work. These heterogeneous reports are not a prediction for a new site. It recommends using experience from earlier afforestation to identify better microsites.

findings.label: Buenavista: intensive production differs from restoration
findings.text: The case in Posadas has rainfall 600–800 mm/year and deeper soils, uses 1 m cubic holes with a 50% cured-cow-manure mixture, and phases planted in autumn 2022/2023. Selected cultivars include Sayalonga, Alexia, P14 and P17, with 10% of the two hermaphrodite cultivars for pollination. Production was not yet measured; the source anticipates 3–4 years. These practices are not recommendations for Almería restoration.

findings.label: An annual area allocation is not a per-event dose
findings.text: Table 5.12 describes establishment/production irrigation below 1500 m³/ha/year for the intensive MP4 model. It is an annual area-based allocation, not L/plant/event; the text does not provide an event count permitting conversion.

findings.label: El Rano: historical management and inconsistent rainfall
findings.text: El Rano (Ubrique, Cádiz) is a longstanding livestock finca with carob, wild olive and family crops. Accessible carobs are grafted and cleared; difficult areas remain seminatural. The narrative gives 800–1200 mm/year rainfall, while Table 5.17 gives 1200–1600. Do not silently choose one or classify it as an Almería case.

browse_groups.maintenance_rule: Organize existing records by their recorded subject. Preserve source contexts and identities; membership is not factual evidence. Community planning values remain separate from source knowledge.
browse_groups.description:
Read watering evidence before selecting a planting example.

1. Nursery: watering before field planting, adapted to substrate, stock and growth or hardening stage.
2. Settlement: the first watering immediately after planting; it is different from all watering over the establishment years.
3. Summer maintenance: recurring watering during a difficult season, with a stated frequency and applicable period.
4. Support: extra water prompted by weather, soil moisture or plant stress. Support can overlap establishment and maintenance; it is not a final age stage.

Amounts and timing: L/plant/event means litres per plant for one watering application. Frequency says how often or what triggers it; period says when in the year; age context distinguishes nursery age from years since field planting. Unknown does not mean zero. A range is not a single recommended dose.

Read the context: soil, rainfall, species, nursery stock size, planting method and access to water affect the regime. Source recommendations, project choices and finca observations have different meanings. Generic LIFE NIEBLAS examples are not species-specific carob recommendations. Evidence does not automatically set a working community's values.

Compare like quantities: 30 L for 100 plants equals an average 0.3 L/plant/event. Container sizes in litres are not doses. A 20 L Cocoon reservoir fill is additional to settlement water. A seasonal total (Las Labores: 400 L/plant over May–September), annual allocation or tank capacity cannot become a per-event dose without sufficient information. No automatic age-based dose curve or stopping age is established.

Glossary: IND/IFWC means individual fog water collector. AFDS means Autonomous Fluid Discharge System: collected water fills a tank and its level triggers discharge through an irrigation network. The maintenance passage uses “SAD” without expanding it; its correspondence with AFDS is a curated interpretation of the matching operation, not a verified acronym expansion. MR means restoration model: MR1 recovers degraded areas; MR2 is oasificación, or restoration using runoff harvesting. MP means production model: MP1 enriches dehesas, MP2 improves older afforestation, MP3 establishes extensive production and MP4 uses intensive production.

Open a phase for quantities, frequency or trigger, season, age context, source limitations and exact-page evidence. Follow its connections to methods and fincas for the practical examples.
